title: Machine-learning test of the single-ion model for $dd$ excitations in cuprates
authors: Maryia Zinouyeva, Leonardo Martinelli, Riccardo Arpaia, Nicholas B. Brookes, Daniele Di Castro, Kurt Kummer, Floriana Lombardi, Giacomo Merzoni, Francesco Rosa, Alessandro Tarasio, Enrico Tassi, Flora Yakhou-Harris, Ezio Puppin, Marco Moretti Sala, Giacomo Ghiringhelli
abstract: We investigate $dd$ excitations in Resonant Inelastic X-ray Scattering spectra of YBa$_2$Cu$_3$O$_6$ and La$_2$CuO$_4$ using the local single-ion model. The data are analyzed by conventional global fitting and by a convolutional neural network trained within the same theoretical framework. For YBa$_2$Cu$_3$O$_6$, the excited state energies obtained with the two methods coincide, leading to the $xy$, $3z^2-r^2$, $xz/yz$ sequence for increasing energy. This result validates the use of machine learning tools for the analysis of RIXS spectra dominated by $dd$ excitations. By contrast, for La$_2$CuO$_4$, the two methods do not converge to a single solution, revealing the limitations of the single-ion model in describing $dd$ excitations in cuprates and pointing to the role of additional contributions beyond a purely local picture in shaping high-energy excitations.
summary: This work analyzes RIXS spectra of cuprates using the single-ion model, comparing results obtained via conventional global fitting and advanced neural network analysis. While the ML approach successfully validates the model for $	ext{YBa}_2	ext{Cu}_3	ext{O}_{6}$, discrepancies found in $	ext{La}_2	ext{CuO}_4$ suggest that describing high-energy excitations requires incorporating physics beyond a purely local picture.
main_problem: The study aims to test the applicability of the local single-ion model for describing $dd$ excitations in cuprate superconductors using Resonant Inelastic X-ray Scattering (RIXS) spectra.
main_result: Agreement between machine learning and conventional fitting methods validates the single-ion picture for YBCO, while discrepancies observed in $	ext{La}_2	ext{CuO}_4$ suggest that additional physics beyond a purely local model is necessary.
method: The analysis combines experimental RIXS data fitting (Global Fitting) with advanced machine learning techniques (Convolutional Neural Networks) trained on synthetic spectra derived from the single-ion Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The system under study is cuprates ($	ext{YBa}_2	ext{Cu}_3	ext{O}_{6}$ and $	ext{La}_2	ext{CuO}_4$), focusing on $dd$ excitations within the $	ext{Cu}\ 3d$ orbitals. The theoretical framework employed is the local single-ion model.
key_observables: Excited state energies ($E_{xy}$, $E_{3z^2-r^2}$, $E_{xz/yz}$), Full Width at Half Maximum (FWHM), and asymmetry parameters ($\alpha$) derived from RIXS spectra.
important_parameters: The analysis depends on scattering geometry, polarization channels ($\sigma 	o \sigma$, etc.), and the distinction between spin-flip ($sf$) and non-spin-flip ($nsf$) contributions.
main_assumptions: Key assumptions include assuming negligible superexchange interaction (equal excitation energy for spin-flip/non-spin-flip) and relying on the single-ion model to describe high-energy excitations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate RIXS spectra measurements under varying scattering geometries ($\phi$ scans, $(\zeta, 0), (\zeta, \zeta)$) comparing experimental data against predictions from both global fitting and neural network models for YBCO and LCO.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the physical problem using RIXS data on two cuprates. It then develops a robust analysis pipeline incorporating machine learning to analyze these spectra, culminating in comparisons that validate the model in one case (YBCO) while highlighting its limitations in another (LCO).
why_interesting: The application of ML/NN techniques to interpret complex spectroscopic data from strongly correlated materials like cuprates is highly relevant. The comparison between different fitting methods provides a rigorous test of theoretical models against experimental reality.

The black curve with white filling shows the difference between the experimental data and the total fit. (c,d) Neural-network (NN) results for the φ scan and (ζ, 0), (ζ, ζ) scans. The NN predicts the peak energies, total FWHMs, and α. These parameters are used to reconstruct the spectrum within the single-ion line-shape model; a common Gaussian width is adjusted for all peaks, while the Lorentzian width of each peak is fixed by the NN-predicted total FWHMs. (e-h) Same as panels (a-d), but for LCO-AF.
